result.title: StimFlow: Synthesizing Brain Activity from Images via Stimulus-conditioned Flow Matching
result.summary: The inherent variability of fMRI responses across trials encourages a generative view of the stimulus-to-response mapping. Prior generative encoders often operate in compressed latent spaces and condition predominantly on semantic features, which provide limited low-level cues for early visual cortex. We propose StimFlow, which synthesizes fMRI directly in native voxel space using conditional flow matching with a linear path. This design aligns training and inference distributions, enabling competitive performance with a single sample and reducing reliance on averaging. To match the visual hierarchy, StimFlow combines structural DINOv2 features with semantic CLIP features, which prove complementary along the cortical processing stream. With a single sample, StimFlow achieves a per-voxel Pearson correlation of 0.371, matching baselines that average five draws. Generation in voxel space allows direct ROI analysis and concept localization without a decoder. Furthermore, it recovers over half of full-data performance from just one hour of scans, supporting efficient cross-subject adaptation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 StimFlow，用条件 flow matching 在原始体素空间直接从图像合成 fMRI 响应，并结合 DINOv2 结构特征与 CLIP 语义特征。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作是脑响应生成/神经编码建模，面向 fMRI 合成与 ROI 分析，不涉及 VLM 的推理状态生成、latent 内容使用或 THINK/LOOK/STOP 类决策，未提供具体可迁移的方法线索。
